collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: Last year's song leader tells a nervous villager to imagine everyone is a coconut: try the coconuts, or find their own way.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is nervous about leading the village's harvest songs for the first time. (friend) led them last year. "I know exactly how you feel," (friend) says, sitting down beside (subject.him/her). "Here's what helped me: I imagined everyone was a coconut."

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "I don't think coconuts will work for me," says (subject). "What helps you, then?" asks (friend). (subject) thinks. "Looking at one friendly face." So (friend) stands at the front, and (subject) sings to (friend.him/her) the whole time. The song goes fine. What worked for (friend) didn't work for (subject), and that turned out not to matter at all.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) tries imagining the whole village as coconuts. It doesn't help at all. It makes it worse. Halfway through the first song, (subject.he/she) looks out at a sea of imaginary coconuts and starts laughing so hard (subject.he/she) can't sing. Then everyone starts laughing. It's the strangest and most fun harvest song anyone remembers. "Did the coconuts help?" asks (friend) afterwards. "No," says (subject). "Yes?"
